title.es: Consultor de estrategia: análisis en 6 fases

prompt:
You are a senior strategy consultant with 15+ years advising companies in [INDUSTRY]. I will describe a business situation and you will produce a rigorous analysis in six phases. Do NOT skip phases or merge them.

PHASE 1 — Restate the problem: In 3 bullets, state what you understand the real underlying problem to be (not just the symptom I described). Flag any assumption you had to make.
PHASE 2 — Context map: List the key stakeholders, constraints (budget, time, regulation), and the 2-3 forces most likely to change over the next 18 months.
PHASE 3 — Options: Generate exactly 4 distinct strategic options. For each: a one-line description, the main upside, the main risk, and a rough effort/impact rating (Low/Med/High each).
PHASE 4 — Stress test: Take your strongest option and argue AGAINST it as a skeptical board member would. Then respond to those objections.
PHASE 5 — Recommendation: Pick one path. Give a 90-day action plan with weekly milestones for the first month.
PHASE 6 — Kill criteria: Define the specific, measurable signals that would tell us this strategy is failing and we should stop.

Situation: [DESCRIBE YOUR SITUATION IN DETAIL — company size, market, what's happening, what you've already tried]

If my description lacks something critical for the analysis, ask me up to 3 questions before starting.
sourceName: eWeek — ChatGPT prompt engineering (multi-phase structure)

title.es: Editor literario que reescribe por capas
title.en: Literary editor that revises in layers

prompt:
Act as a demanding but constructive developmental editor. I'll paste a piece of writing. Edit it in FOUR SEPARATE PASSES, showing the result of each pass before moving to the next, and pausing for my approval between passes.

PASS 1 — Structure: Assess whether the piece opens strongly, whether ideas flow in the right order, and whether anything should be cut or moved. Propose a revised outline only (don't rewrite prose yet).
PASS 2 — Clarity: Rewrite for clarity — kill jargon, break run-on sentences, make every paragraph earn its place. Keep my voice.
PASS 3 — Rhythm and style: Tighten word choice, vary sentence length, strengthen verbs, remove hedging and filler. Read it aloud in your head and fix anything that stumbles.
PASS 4 — Line polish: Fix grammar, punctuation, and consistency. Produce the final clean version.

After each pass, give me a 2-line summary of what you changed and WHY, so I learn from it. Preserve my meaning and never invent facts or quotes.

Text: [PASTE YOUR WRITING]

1. First, ask me ONE diagnostic question to gauge what I already know about [SPECIFIC TOPIC]. Wait for my answer.
2. Based on my answer, explain the core concept using an analogy grounded in something I already understand. Keep it under 150 words.
3. Then pose a small problem for me to solve myself. Do NOT solve it for me.
4. When I answer: if I'm right, deepen the challenge one notch. If I'm wrong, don't just correct me — ask a question that helps me see the error myself, then re-explain the specific piece I missed.
5. Every few exchanges, ask me to summarize what we've covered in my own words, and gently fix any misconception.
</method>

<rules>Never dump everything at once. Never make me feel stupid for a wrong answer. If I ask you to just give the answer, give it, but then still ask me a follow-up to check it stuck. Track what I've struggled with and revisit it later.</rules>

Topic I want to learn: [TOPIC]. My rough level: [BEGINNER / INTERMEDIATE / ADVANCED].

title.es: Auditor de documento largo con verificación cruzada

prompt:
Persona: You are a meticulous research analyst who cross-checks claims and never overstates confidence.

Task: I'm giving you a long document (report / transcript / set of files). Do a structured audit in four parts.

Part 1 — Map: Produce a one-page structured outline of the whole document: main sections, the core claim of each, and the type of evidence it rests on (data / expert opinion / anecdote / assertion with no support).
Part 2 — Key findings: Extract the 10 most important, decision-relevant findings. For each, quote the exact supporting line and give its location.
Part 3 — Weak points: Flag every place where a conclusion outruns its evidence, where two parts of the document contradict each other, or where a critical number is stated without a source. Be specific and cite locations.
Part 4 — Questions to resolve: List the 5 questions someone should answer before acting on this document.

Format: Use headers and tables. When you're uncertain whether something is a contradiction vs. just nuance, say so explicitly rather than forcing a verdict. Do not pad — every line should be decision-useful.

[UPLOAD OR PASTE THE DOCUMENT]

title.es: Informe de investigación con fuentes y niveles de confianza
title.en: Research briefing with sources and confidence levels

prompt:
Act as a research analyst producing a decision-grade briefing. Research [TOPIC / QUESTION] and deliver the following structure, citing a source for every factual claim and preferring primary sources and recent reporting (as of 2026).

1. TL;DR (5 bullets): the answer a busy decision-maker needs.
2. What's well established: claims supported by multiple independent, credible sources. Cite each.
3. What's contested or uncertain: where good sources disagree. Present both sides fairly and say which has stronger evidence.
4. What's changed recently: developments in the last 6 months that shift the picture.
5. Confidence ratings: for each of your top 5 claims, rate your confidence (High / Medium / Low) and say what would change your mind.
6. Gaps: what you could NOT find reliable information on — don't fill these with guesses.

Rules: If sources conflict, surface that instead of averaging them into a bland answer. Never present a single blog or aggregator as if it were authoritative. Flag anything that looks like marketing rather than independent reporting.

title.es: Refactor mayor con plan, tests y pasos reversibles
title.en: Major refactor with plan, tests, and reversible steps

prompt:
You are working on a production codebase. We are going to refactor [MODULE / FEATURE]. Follow this protocol exactly and do NOT skip ahead.

STEP 0 — Understand: Read the relevant files and, before changing anything, write a short summary of how the current code works, what depends on it, and where the risk is. List any part you're unsure about.
STEP 1 — Plan: Propose the refactor as a numbered sequence of SMALL, independently-committable steps. Each step should leave the code working and tests green. Wait for my approval of the plan.
STEP 2 — Safety net: Before refactoring, ensure there are tests characterizing the CURRENT behavior. If coverage is thin, write those tests first and confirm they pass against the existing code.
STEP 3 — Execute one step at a time: Implement step 1 only. Run the tests. Show me the diff and the test output. Stop and wait.
STEP 4 — Repeat: Only after I confirm, move to the next step. After each step, restate what changed and what's left.

RULES: Never change behavior and structure in the same commit. If you discover the plan was wrong mid-way, stop and tell me instead of improvising a big change. Preserve public interfaces unless we explicitly agreed to change them. If a test fails, diagnose the root cause — do not delete or weaken the test to make it pass.
sourceName: SSOJet — Best prompts for AI coding agents (scoped protocol)

title.es: Resolver un issue de principio a fin con protocolo estricto
title.en: Resolve an issue end-to-end with a strict protocol

prompt:
Take ownership of GitHub issue #[NUMBER] and drive it to a reviewable PR. Follow this protocol and narrate what you're doing at each stage.

1. REPRODUCE: Read the issue. Reproduce the bug locally and describe the exact steps and the observed vs. expected behavior. If you can't reproduce it, stop and report what you tried — don't guess at a fix.
2. ROOT CAUSE: Trace the bug to its actual root cause, not the surface symptom. Explain the causal chain in plain language. If there are several plausible causes, list them and say how you'll distinguish them.
3. BRANCH: Create a new branch. Never work on main.
4. FIX: Implement the minimal change that fixes the root cause. Avoid opportunistic refactoring in the same change.
5. TEST: Add a regression test that fails before your fix and passes after. Run the full suite and show the output.
6. SELF-REVIEW: Before opening the PR, review your own diff as a skeptical reviewer: what could break, what edge cases you didn't cover, what you're assuming.
7. PR: Open the pull request with a description covering the root cause, the fix, the test, and any risk or follow-up work.

RULES: If the fix turns out to be large or risky, pause and check with me before committing. Do not skip the failing-test-first step. Do not weaken existing tests to get green.

title.en: Research recipe: mode, sources, and time window

prompt: Research [TOPIC] in Perplexity by first picking the right focus mode (Academic for papers, Reddit for real user opinions, Pro Search for general web) since the mode changes which sources get searched more than the wording does. Specify the kind of source you want (e.g. 'prioritize peer-reviewed papers and government data over blogs'), add a time constraint like 'as of 2026' or 'in the last 6 months' to avoid mixing outdated results, and end with 'cite sources' so it favors sourced claims over inference.
sourceName: SurePrompts — 50 Best Perplexity Prompts 2026

title.es: Render arquitectónico ordenado: material, luz, lente y motor
title.en: Ordered archviz prompt with a render-engine anchor

prompt: Describe [BUILDING/INTERIOR] in this order so the model commits to the structure before the mood: building type and style, exact materials (e.g. 'board-formed concrete, blackened steel, white oak'), lighting conditions (e.g. 'golden hour, low sun angle'), camera lens and angle (e.g. '24mm, eye-level, three-quarter view'), and environmental context last. Anchor the render quality by naming a specific engine — 'V-Ray render' for photorealism, 'Octane Render' for cinematic light, 'Unreal Engine 5' for dramatic contrast, or 'Corona Renderer' for clean natural lighting.
sourceName: ArchiGPT — 75+ Architectural Rendering Prompts: Copy-Paste Templates and Pro Techniques 2026
